text: The pivotal sentence of Genesis 6 concerns God's inner life. Yahweh sees that every imagination of the human heart is only evil continually (6:5), he is sorry that he made man, and he is grieved in his heart (6:6). The grief comes before the sentence of judgment and gives it its character. What moves the flood is a maker's sorrow over what his creatures have become. Before any rain falls, the first covenant in Scripture appears. God promises to establish his covenant with Noah, who is to come into the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives (6:18). The promise reaches past Noah to the animals, two of every sort (6:19), and to the food that will keep them all alive (6:21). The chapter that announces the end of all flesh (6:13) also arranges, in some detail, what will survive it. Noah, the one man who found favor in the eyes of Yahweh (6:8), is told to gather in the creatures God is about to drown.
